newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-PONTING STEERS TASMANIA TO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PONTING STEERS TASMANIA TO VICTORY.

text.p: Discarded Australia test batsman Ricky Ponting scored a century in each innings to steer Tasmania to a five-wicket win over South Australia in their Sheffield Shield match on Friday.

Ponting, overlooked for Australia's current tour of South Africa, hit an unbeaten 145 as Tasmania, set a winning target of 349, reached 351 for five in their second innings at Hobart's Bellerive Oval.
The victory lifted Tasmania to second place on the Sheffield Shield table behind leaders Western Australia. The top two sides qualify for next month's final.
South Australia captain Jamie Siddons had declared his side's second innings on 209 for five before lunch on the fourth and final day.

Ponting, who made 126 in Tasmania's first innings, hit 15 boundaries and faced 194 deliveries in a performance that must have enhanced his prospects of selection for the Ashes tour to England later this year.

In Perth, Western Australia batsman Murray Goodwin scored an unbeaten 125, his maiden first-class century, to help the home side to 317 for three at close of play on the first day of their match against Queensland.
